$comment: Which core capabilities must exist in which ports, and where each port keeps them.
Checked by release/check-parity.sh, which fails when a required capability has no file.
This is a DECLARATION, not a derivation: 'whatever TypeScript has' is the wrong rule.
Ports legitimately differ in shape — canonical_json exists in six ports and not in
TypeScript (whose JSON.stringify IS the reference), and Rust and Go split value/handler/
offsets out of modules TypeScript keeps whole. What must not differ is capability.
An intentionally single-port capability carries a `why`. Anything undeclared is drift.
Adding a port means adding it to `ports` and giving every required capability a path.
$comment_kotlin: Kotlin has no core of its own — java/kotlin and java/kotest sit on the Java core.

capabilities.name: execute
capabilities.what: runs a planned example and compares sensor returns

capabilities.name: failure-anchor
capabilities.what: where a failure points: the failing cell's span, else the step's

capabilities.name: run-result-payload
capabilities.what: the .varar/<oath>.json types and their wire projection (ADR 0014)

capabilities.name: failure-producer
capabilities.what: a caught step failure → the run-result failure payload

capabilities.name: conformance-artifacts
capabilities.what: the doc/registry/plan/trace projections the corpus compares

capabilities.name: run-diagnostics
capabilities.why: TypeScript only, on purpose: one language server serves every language, and it is written in TypeScript. The other ports produce run results (see run-result-payload); only this port renders them.

capabilities.name: canonical-json
capabilities.what: key-sorted JSON, byte-identical to JSON.stringify(sortKeys(v), null, 2)
capabilities.why: Absent from TypeScript on purpose: its JSON.stringify IS the reference the other six reproduce.
